name: Munnar
tagline: Rolling tea estates high in the Western Ghats.
whenBlurb: September to March is cool, green and clear across the tea country; the southwest monsoon closes in from June to August, and the rare Neelakurinji bloom returns around 2030.

ourTake.lede: Munnar is a landscape rather than a sightseeing town, so resist the packaged 'point-to-point' viewpoint circuit that clogs the roads and instead stay high on a working tea estate and walk. The mornings, before the valley mist burns off, are the magic; the afternoons often cloud over. Skip the crowded central town and the manufactured 'photo points'; the real Munnar is the silence of the plantations.
ourTake.comeIf: You want rolling tea hills and cool air within a short drive of the Kerala coast.
ourTake.skipIf: You want beaches or nightlife; this is a quiet, high-country tea town.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Lockhart Bungalow, a CGH Earth SAHA Experience
credentials: CGH Earth, a SAHA (heritage-home) Experience, the group's Munnar address
Restored 1940s British planter's bungalow, 3 rooms only
Within the ~1,500-acre Lockhart tea estate
items.description: CGH Earth's 1940s planter's bungalow, just three rooms, set within a 1,500-acre working tea estate, looking down on rolling hills and gardens.

items.name: Windermere Estate
credentials: Featured by Scott Dunn, Rare India, Secret Retreats, Kuoni and Audley Travel
18-room estate home on a 1940s cardamom, coffee and tea plantation
Perched on Observatory Hill, in the Palni/Western Ghats
items.description: An 18-room plantation retreat on a 1940s cardamom-and-coffee estate, high on Observatory Hill, 360-degree views that often look down on the clouds.

items.name: Fragrant Nature Munnar
credentials: Five Star Classified hotel
~43 rooms across five categories, most with authentic in-room fireplaces
Multi-cuisine and speciality dining, spa
items.description: A Five Star Classified resort of colonial style over rolling valleys, most of its rooms carry a real in-room fireplace for the cool hill nights.

items.name: SpiceTree Munnar
credentials: Award-winning design-led boutique; featured by Wexas Travel (UK luxury operator)
Listed by Kerala Tourism
14 suites + 2 private pool villas with solar-heated infinity pools
items.description: The hills' most design-led boutique, 14 suites and two pool villas with solar-heated infinity pools and Victorian copper tubs, each framing forest and valley.

items.name: The Tall Trees Munnar
credentials: WGH Hotels & Resorts
26 individual cottages across 66 acres of Shola forest
Pool with jacuzzi; glass-roofed forest restaurant
items.description: Twenty-six individual cottages scattered across 66 acres of Shola forest under 600-odd towering trees, with a forest restaurant beneath a transparent roof.

items.name: Parakkat Nature Hotels & Resorts
credentials: Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice
~80 rooms from classic to pool villa suites
Spa, multiple pools, panoramic tea-estate views
items.description: A large tea-view resort with pool villa suites, a spa and a zipline, Munnar's most decorated crowd-pleaser, over panoramic plantations.

items.name: Chandys Windy Woods
credentials: Listed by Kerala Tourism
Hillside blocks with mountain-view balconies
Outdoor pool, spa and wellness centre
items.description: A quietly chic hillside resort of grey stone and white walls stepped down the slope, muted, calm and plantation-facing.

items.name: Ambady Estate
credentials: Boutique chalets and a private villa within a certified organic cardamom plantation
Two-level chalets with stone fireplaces
Consistently rated for cleanliness and personal service
items.description: A handful of split-level chalets and a private villa set within a certified organic cardamom plantation, stone fireplaces and old-world calm.

items.name: Eravikulam National Park & the Nilgiri Tahr
credentials: Western Ghats, UNESCO World Heritage Site
World's largest Nilgiri tahr population
items.description: The single most important place in the high ranges, 97 sq km of rolling shola-grassland that holds the world's largest surviving population of the endangered Nilgiri tahr, the wild mountain goat that walks up to visitors on the Rajamalai trail. Entry is by forest-department shuttle only and the daily quota is tight, so a private guide books the first slot and has you on the misty grassland before the buses arrive.

items.name: Anamudi, the highest peak in South India
credentials: Highest peak in South India, 2,695 m
Western Ghats, UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: At 2,695 metres, Anamudi is the tallest mountain anywhere in India south of the Himalaya, its shola-crowned summit rising above the tahr grasslands of Eravikulam. The peak itself is protected and closed to casual climbers, but from the Rajamalai road it fills the horizon, a quiet, humbling anchor to any high-ranges trip.

items.name: The Neelakurinji bloom (once in twelve years)
credentials: Blooms once every 12 years, next in 2030
Western Ghats, UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: Once every twelve years the shola grasslands turn a rolling sea of violet-blue as the Neelakurinji flower blooms in unison, a spectacle that last carpeted these hills in 2018 and returns in 2030. It is one of the rarest natural events on the subcontinent; families plan whole journeys around the July-to-October window, and a good advisor secures the park permits months ahead.

items.name: Kannan Devan / Tata Tea Museum
items.description: The story of how the British and then Tata turned these hills into the great Kannan Devan tea country, told inside a working estate, antique rollers, a curling machine, the old Pelton wheel, and a demonstration room where you watch fresh leaf become the cup. A five-minute drive from town and the natural first stop before you set out among the plantations.

items.name: A private tea-tasting & estate walk (Kannan Devan hills)
items.description: The rolling emerald plantations that made Munnar famous are best met on foot, a guided walk between the clipped tea bushes at dawn, the pluckers moving through the mist, ending with a proper tasting of single-estate leaf. A concierge arranges a private estate walk with a plantation manager rather than the crowded roadside stops.

items.name: Tea-plucking with the estate workers
items.description: A hands-on morning in the gardens, a basket, a guide, and the surprisingly precise 'two leaves and a bud' technique the women pluckers have perfected over generations. Genuinely charming for children and grandparents alike, and the kind of unhurried, grounding experience the luxury tea-bungalows arrange privately for their guests.

items.name: Mattupetty Dam & Lake (boating)
items.area: 13 km from Munnar, towards Top Station
items.description: A concrete-gravity dam holding a still, tea-fringed lake where the tourism department runs pedal-boats, speedboats and slow shikara-style rides, and where elephants sometimes come down to the banks in the early morning. An easy, pretty half-day on the classic Munnar circuit, best just after sunrise before the day-trippers arrive.

items.name: Kundala Lake & Dam
items.area: 20 km from Munnar, towards Top Station
items.description: A quiet high-altitude reservoir cradled by tea slopes and, in season, the rare Neelakurinji, famous for its pedal-boats and a genuinely lovely dawn-and-dusk light on the water. Calmer and less crowded than Mattupetty, it is the one to send a couple to for a slow, misty hour on the lake.

items.name: Top Station (the valley view & the state border)
items.area: 32 km from Munnar, on the Kerala–Tamil Nadu border
items.description: At around 1,700 metres this is the highest point on the Munnar road and its finest lookout, a viewing deck that spills out over the Theni valley of Tamil Nadu, clouds pouring up the escarpment below your feet. Go early; by mid-morning the mist often closes in and the great view is gone.

items.name: Echo Point
items.area: 15 km from Munnar, towards Top Station
items.description: A lakeside bend in the hills where a shout comes back to you off the far ridges, a simple, joyful stop that children adore, set on a serene stretch of water ringed by tea and forest. Part of the classic circuit; pair it with Mattupetty and Kundala on the same drive.

items.name: Photo Point
items.description: Exactly what the name promises, a curated bend where a stream runs through rows of tea and tall trees frame the classic postcard of Munnar. Touristy but genuinely photogenic, and a quick, pretty pause on the way in or out of the plantations.

items.name: Pothamedu Viewpoint
items.area: 3 km from Munnar town, on the Kochi road
items.description: One of the great panoramas of the high ranges, undulating tea, cardamom and coffee slopes falling away to a river valley, with the whole Western Ghats stacked in blue layers behind. Close to town, uncrowded, and a favourite of the honeymoon crowd for its sunset light.

items.name: Attukal Waterfalls
items.area: Between Pallivasal and Munnar, 9 km from town
items.description: A frothing white cascade that tumbles over rocks through a wooded gorge, its spray hanging in the tea-country mist, best in and just after the monsoon when it runs full. An easy roadside stop with a short walk to the viewpoint, lovely for photographs on the way into the plantations.

items.name: Lakkam Waterfalls
items.description: Fed by the Eravikulam plateau, this fall drops off a rock shelf into a clear pool and is one of the few around Munnar where you can safely dip your feet in a shallow, cordoned bathing area. Set on the Marayoor road, it pairs neatly with a day trip to the sandalwood country.

items.name: Chinnakanal (Power House) Waterfalls
items.description: Known locally as the Power House Falls, this steep, powerful cascade of the Devikulam stream thunders down a cliff face and is at its most dramatic in monsoon. A short stop en route to the Anayirankal reservoir and the Chinnakanal viewpoints on the Thekkady side of Munnar.

items.name: Pallivasal (Kerala's first hydel project)
items.description: The very first hydroelectric scheme in Kerala, set among forested slopes and a pretty falls, history and scenery in one quiet, uncrowded stop that most day-trippers skip. Worth the short detour on the way to or from Attukal.

items.name: CSI Christ Church (1910)
items.description: A little stone Anglican church built in 1910 for the British planters, one of the few colonial buildings to survive the catastrophic 1924 floods that redrew Munnar, its worn brass plaques and stained glass still telling the story of the tea pioneers. A serene, ten-minute stop that grounds the whole hill station in its history.

items.name: Blossom Hydel Park
items.description: An 18-acre riverside park laid out below the hills, with landscaped walks, cycling tracks, boating and skating, the easy, in-town green space for families with young children. Not the reason you come to Munnar, but a pleasant hour when a multi-generation group wants a gentle morning close to the hotel.

items.name: The Rose Garden
items.description: A sprawling hillside garden of roses, fruit orchards and spice plants where you can wander among the beds, watch honey-bees at work and taste estate-grown fruit, a soft, sensory stop that older children and grandparents enjoy. Modest and unhurried; a nice counterpoint to the big viewpoints.

items.name: A cardamom & spice plantation walk
items.description: The high ranges are cardamom country, and a walk through a working spice estate, cardamom, pepper, clove, nutmeg, vanilla climbing through the shade trees, is a fragrant, tactile way to understand what these hills actually grow. The luxury estate-stays run private plantation walks with a resident naturalist.

items.name: Marayoor sandalwood forest
items.description: The only natural sandalwood forest in Kerala, some sixty thousand wild sandalwood trees on a dry, sunlit plateau utterly different from misty Munnar, guarded by the forest department against poachers. A guided drive through the reserve, with the resinous scent of the trees in the air, is one of the region's most distinctive half-days.

items.name: The Marayoor dolmens (Muniyaras)
items.description: Scattered across the Marayoor plateau are Iron Age burial chambers, four stones on edge under a great capstone, and Stone Age rock paintings, some of the oldest human traces in South India. A quiet, extraordinary stop for a history-minded family, easily combined with the sandalwood forest and jaggery villages.

items.name: Marayoor jaggery villages
credentials: Marayoor jaggery, GI-tagged (Geographical Indication)
items.description: The sugarcane of Marayoor makes a dark, mineral-rich jaggery so prized it carries a Geographical Indication tag, and you can watch it being boiled and moulded in the small family units by the roadside. A warm, authentic taste of the plateau; buy a block straight from the makers.

items.name: Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary
credentials: Western Ghats, UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: A dry, thorn-forest sanctuary on the rain-shadow side of the Ghats, utterly unlike Munnar's tea slopes, famous for the grizzled giant squirrel, star tortoise, elephant and the highest reptile diversity in Kerala. A guided trek to the Thoovanam Waterfalls through the deciduous forest is the classic Chinnar day.

items.name: Anamudi Shola National Park
credentials: Western Ghats, UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: A compact but precious park of montane shola forest and grassland below Anamudi, threaded with quiet trails and home to Nilgiri tahr, marten and rare shola birds. Far less visited than Eravikulam, it is the one to send a serious walker or birder to for solitude among the mist-forest.

items.name: Anayirankal Dam & reservoir
items.description: One of Kerala's largest earthen dams, its still reservoir ringed by tea gardens and evergreen forest, with elephants regularly crossing the far shore, hence the name, 'where elephants descend'. Boating and a picnic on the grassy bank make it a lovely, low-key stop on the Thekkady road.

items.name: Chinnakanal & the elephant country
items.description: A stretch of high grassland and tea where wild elephant herds move between the forest and the reservoir, dotted with viewpoints and the well-known Power House falls. It is where several of the finest estate-stays sit; a naturalist-led drive at dusk is the way to see the herds respectfully.

items.name: Kolukkumalai, the world's highest tea estate, at sunrise
items.area: ~32 km from Munnar, across the Tamil Nadu border (Theni)
credentials: World's highest tea plantation, ~2,150 m
items.description: At about 2,150 metres this is the highest tea plantation on earth, reached only by a rugged 4x4 jeep climb in the pre-dawn dark, and the reward is a sunrise that breaks over a literal sea of clouds filling the valleys below. The 1930s factory still makes tea the slow orthodox way. The single most memorable morning in the high ranges; the concierge arranges a private jeep and the sunrise slot.

items.name: Meesapulimala trek (second-highest peak in South India)
credentials: Second-highest peak in South India, 2,640 m
Western Ghats, UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: A full-day trek across eight rolling shola-grassland peaks to the 2,640-metre summit of Meesapulimala, the second-highest in South India, with 360-degree views over the Ghats and the Tamil Nadu plains. Permitted only through the forest department's eco-programme; a fit family can do it in a day, or stay overnight in the Rhodo Valley tented camp.

items.name: Thekkady & the Periyar Tiger Reserve
credentials: Periyar Tiger Reserve, Project Tiger reserve
items.description: The great wildlife day-trip from the high ranges, a 925 sq km tiger reserve around a forest lake, where a quiet boat cruise or a guided bamboo-raft trip brings elephant, gaur, sambar and, for the lucky, the tiger itself down to the water. Pair it with a Thekkady spice-plantation walk; many families make it an overnight rather than a rushed day.

items.name: Vagamon (the meadows & pine forests)
items.description: A gentler, greener hill station of rolling meadows, planted pine forests and a famous paragliding valley, softer and more open than Munnar's steep tea country. A scenic day-drive or an alternate base for a family wanting quiet walks, the pine avenue and the Kurisumala pilgrimage hill.

items.name: Ethical elephant experience
items.description: Wild elephants belong to these hills, and the responsible way to meet them is by observation, a naturalist drive through Chinnakanal and Anayirankal where herds cross the tea, rather than the roadside 'rides' the estates now steer guests away from. A good advisor books only welfare-first, observation-based encounters.

items.name: Guided birding in the shola forests
credentials: Western Ghats, UNESCO World Heritage Site & global biodiversity hotspot
items.description: The Western Ghats are one of the world's birding hotspots, and the high ranges hold endemics found nowhere else, the Nilgiri wood-pigeon, Nilgiri flycatcher, white-bellied shortwing and Kerala laughingthrush among them. An early guided morning with a specialist naturalist is a quiet, rewarding counterpoint to the sightseeing circuit.

items.name: Lockhart Gap & the tea-country drive
items.area: On the Munnar–Kochi road, ~25 km from town
items.description: A dramatic mountain pass where the road threads between sheer green ridges and the valley falls away in tiers of tea, one of the most cinematic stretches of the whole approach to Munnar. A natural photo-stop, and the gap where the clouds famously pour over the ridge in the afternoon.

items.name: Sita Devi Lake (Devikulam)
items.description: A small, mineral-spring lake wrapped in tea slopes and legend, said in the Ramayana to be where Sita bathed, quiet, uncrowded and pretty for a slow walk and a few photographs. A gentle stop for a couple wanting somewhere off the main circuit.

items.name: Kanthalloor (the fruit-orchard village)
items.description: A cool, high village of apple, orange, plum and gooseberry orchards and terraced vegetable farms, 'the Kashmir of Kerala', set in the same dry-plateau country as Marayoor. A rewarding add-on to the sandalwood day, especially in fruiting season when you can pick straight from the trees.

items.name: Devikulam & the old British plantation trail
items.description: One of the oldest planter settlements in the hills, its lanes still lined with colonial-era estate bungalows, a little club and mist-wrapped tea gardens, quiet, atmospheric and steeped in the story of British Munnar. Best explored on foot with a guide who knows the planters' history.

items.name: A stay at Windermere Estate
items.description: An eighteen-room planter's-bungalow retreat perched on a hilltop inside a working cardamom and coffee estate, with 360-degree views that often look down onto the clouds. The archetypal Munnar tea-country stay, intimate, unhurried, veg-friendly Kerala kitchens and estate walks from the door.

items.name: A stay at SpiceTree Munnar
items.description: A boutique retreat of just sixteen suites and pool villas high above Chinnakanal, built for privacy and the long valley views, heated pools, glass-walled rooms in the mist, and elephant country on the doorstep. The choice for a couple or a small family wanting the most polished modern-luxury base in the high ranges.

items.name: A stay at KTDC Tea County
items.description: Kerala Tourism's premium hill resort, tucked between two tea-clad hills a short walk from town, with cottages, a spa and easy access to trekking, cycling and the plantations. A reliable, well-located classic for a multi-generation group that wants comfort close to the sights.

items.name: A guided plantation-country trek
credentials: Western Ghats, UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: The finest way to feel the high ranges is on foot, a half-day walk through tea, shola pockets and grassland ridges with a naturalist, ending at a viewpoint no vehicle reaches. Routes scale from a gentle estate loop for grandparents to a proper ridge hike for teenagers; the estate-stays and forest department both arrange guides.

items.name: Cloud-watching at dawn from a high viewpoint
items.description: The signature magic of Munnar is the morning cloud-sea, valleys brimming with mist that the rising sun turns gold before it burns away by nine. Whether from a private estate deck or a jeep at Kolukkumalai, an unhurried dawn with a flask of estate tea is the quiet luxury this hill country does best.

items.name: Munnar town market & the tea-and-spice buying
items.description: The little bazaar in town is where the estate teas, cardamom, pepper, homemade chocolate and eucalyptus oil come together, a good hour to buy genuine single-estate leaf and freshly graded cardamom to carry home. A guide steers you to the honest sellers rather than the tourist-priced stalls.

items.name: Nyayamakad Waterfalls
items.area: Between Munnar and Rajamalai, ~10 km from town
items.description: A long, misty veil of water dropping over a rock face beside the Eravikulam road, at its full glory in and just after the monsoon, an easy roadside pause you pass on the way to the national park. Pretty, uncrowded and perfectly timed with an early Eravikulam visit.

items.name: Ayurvedic spa & tea-bath ritual
items.description: Kerala is the home of Ayurveda, and the high-ranges estate-stays wrap it in the local tea, warm oil abhyanga, herbal steam and green-tea-and-spice bath rituals after a day on the ridges. The most restorative way to end a trekking or sightseeing day, and a natural indulgence for a honeymoon.

items.name: Lockhart Bungalow table
credentials: The dining table of Lockhart Bungalow, a CGH Earth SAHA Experience
Estate-grown, home-style Kerala meals
items.description: CGH Earth's estate kitchen, home-style Kerala cooking from the plantation, eaten in a 1940s bungalow with the tea hills below.

items.name: Fragrant Nature Munnar restaurants
credentials: In-house dining at a Five Star Classified hotel
Multi-cuisine restaurant plus a speciality grill room
items.description: The hills' most complete resort dining, a multi-cuisine room and a grill speciality restaurant, with valley views and fireplaces.

items.name: Saravana Bhavan, Munnar
credentials: Branch of the global Saravana Bhavan pure-vegetarian chain
A dependable, veg/Jain-friendly table in the town centre
items.description: The Munnar branch of the world's best-known pure-vegetarian South Indian chain, dosas, idlis and filter coffee, done right.

items.name: Rapsy Restaurant
credentials: Widely cited as Munnar town's best-loved local restaurant (Tripadvisor, Kerala food guides)
Known for parottas, biryani and its multi-country breakfast board
items.description: Munnar's most-recommended local room, famous for parottas, biryani and the day's Kerala plates, packed at lunch with residents.

items.name: SN Restaurant
credentials: One of the oldest established restaurants in Munnar town
Known for authentic, affordable Kerala meals and fish curry
items.description: One of Munnar's oldest eating houses, plain, authentic Kerala meals and fish-curry plates in the heart of town.

items.name: Resort bars & fireside lounges
credentials: In-house bars and fireside lounges at the leading Munnar resorts
Fireplaces, terraces and cool-evening nightcaps
items.description: The honest answer to Munnar after dark, a fireside lounge or terrace bar at Fragrant Nature, Parakkat or Chandys, with a nightcap and the cold coming down.

items.name: SpiceTree Munnar bar & deck
credentials: In-resort bar at a design-led boutique
Deck and lounge over forest and valley
items.description: The most designed evening in the hills, a considered drink on a boutique deck over the forest and valley, away from the town.

items.name: Estate bonfire & evening at Windermere Estate
credentials: Plantation-estate evenings at Windermere Estate
Bonfires and terrace drinks in the cool hill air
items.description: The truest Munnar evening, a bonfire and a quiet drink on a plantation hilltop as the mist settles and the temperature drops.

plan.heading: 3 days in Munnar, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Arrive and settle at SwaSwara-calibre calm, the tented luxury of the Kolukkumalai ridge or a private tea-estate bungalow, with a slow lunch overlooking the slopes.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A guided walk through a working tea garden with a planter, learning the pluck and the flush by hand rather than by placard.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A fireside dinner of estate-grown produce, with the valley going dark below.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: An early drive to Kolukkumalai, the world's highest tea estate, for the sunrise above the cloud line and the vintage roller-mill still in use.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Eravikulam National Park slopes for the Nilgiri tahr, timed for the quiet window, then Mattupetty dam and the shola forest edge.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner back at the estate, paired with single-origin Munnar teas after.

days.label: Day 3
days.title: Tea, table and the road down

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Tata Tea Museum for the machinery and the tasting, then a private cupping session to fix a blend to take home.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A gentle plantation trek to a lookout with a packed estate lunch, ending in the afternoon light on the terraces.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final dinner of Kerala highland cooking before an early night ahead of the drive out.

items.name: High estate belt (above the town)
items.description: Bungalows and lodges among the plantations; best for views, walks and quiet.

items.name: Munnar town
items.description: The functional centre with shops and budget stays; convenient but busy and best avoided as a base.

items.name: Chinnakanal / Anachal (approach road)
items.description: Resorts on the way up with valley views; for comfort with easy access.

events.name: Neelakurinji bloom
events.note: The hills turn blue-violet when the rare kurinji flowers en masse; a genuine once-in-a-cycle event.

events.name: Onam
events.note: Kerala's harvest festival is celebrated warmly on the estates, with feasts and floral decorations.

events.name: Peak clear-weather season
events.note: The post-monsoon and dry-winter windows give the clearest tea-country light and best walking.

events.name: Christmas & New Year
events.note: The estates and resorts fill with a festive high-season crowd; charming but book far ahead.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Nights are cool at 1,600 metres, so pack a warm layer even in summer; stay on a working tea estate for the finest setting, and avoid the peak monsoon months of June to August when landslides can close roads.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Cochin International Airport (COK), then a scenic four-hour chauffeured drive up into the Western Ghats; the road climbs through tea country.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car with driver is essential for the winding hill roads and estate visits; short walks through the tea gardens and to the viewpoints on foot.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Jio and Airtel 4G is patchy in the higher estates and valleys, so download maps and expect quiet stretches; hotel wifi is the dependable line.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee; larger resorts take cards, but carry cash for small estates, spice stalls and viewpoint stops; tipping drivers and guides is customary.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: September to March is the window, cool and clear at 1,600m with the tea hills at their greenest; avoid June-August, when monsoon rain triggers landslides and shuts viewpoints.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No airport; fly to Cochin International (COK), then a 3-hour drive up NH85 (about 108 km). Reach COK direct from Delhi, Mumbai or Bengaluru on IndiGo/Air India, or via a Gulf hub in business/first, then have your advisor arrange a car with a driver who knows the ghat road.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: Altitude is a gentle 1,600m, no acclimatisation needed. No special vaccinations beyond routine cover. Very safe; the main caution is the winding hill drive and slippery roads in the wet. Drink sealed or filtered water.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Effortless: Kerala hill fare is heavily vegetarian, and every resort does South Indian and North Indian veg. Jain is understood at the better properties if flagged ahead. The plantation-estate kitchens (Windermere, Tea Sanctuary) do refined vegetarian food.
